acceptance: Measure queue depth and wait per workflow for one week; identify runs that add no signal (superseded heads, duplicate extension-smoke, cancelled-but-queued) and add concurrency cancellation or path filters; decide on runner capacity. Report median core wait before and after.
context: 2026-10-31 evidence (session on CI time): the queue is mostly CI, not oracle. A CI run executes about 22 jobs and about 4,300 runner-seconds per pull-request event; oracle work uses about 2 runner-minutes per event, so CI is about 97% of runner time. Between 11:23 and 15:17 UTC there were 122 pull-request events against 8 develop pushes, with 54 open pull requests. By run count about 125 of 205 queued runs were oracle workflows, but they take almost no runner time. The queue drained to 0 by 2026-11-01 13:06 UTC. Editing oracle workflows to shrink it was reviewed and judged unsafe (see oracle-gate-bridge-noop-runs-hold-runner-slots-20261101). Options with no gate risk: cap open pull requests or concurrent pushes, avoid ready_for_review in the same second as a push (oracle-verdict-same-second-push-and-ready-cancels-new-head-20261101), and reduce ci.yml fan-out (ci.yml is a soundness path). The owner chose not to change runner capacity; the Free plan pool is 20 jobs.
description: Observed 2026-10-31: 59-128 queued workflow runs with 1-6 in progress; later 197 queued and 0 in progress at 15:32Z, oldest queued run from 11:50Z. pr-arm refuses until core records the verify-fast-duration verdict, so each push (including GitHub "Update branch" merges, which also restart oracle review) restarts a multi-hour wait. Six release-UAT fix PRs took from about 07:30Z to 14:11Z to merge once their CI was fixed; later fixes waited 5+ h more. Queue contributors include about 30 concurrent QuestDB PRs from one session and per-PR oracle and extension-smoke runs.
